findings.source_passage: My dark world was slowly receding, and that was my introduction back into the real one. I forced my eyes open and was presented with a barren sight.
findings.source_locator: Opening paragraphs, after the first line of dialogue
findings.why_it_matters: The narrator's wry, detached voice—'that was my introduction back into the real one' and 'presented with a barren sight'—establishes her register immediately; the draft collapses this into bland functional prose ('The voice hauled me back. I pried my eyes open').
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the narrator's dry, slightly formal self-commentary in the first-person orientation sentence to preserve the voice register that defines the chapter's POV.

findings.source_passage: Tears had run her makeup down her face and given her an undead look.
findings.source_locator: Description of the irate woman, before 'Let me out, you stupid fucks!'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'undead look' simile is the narrator's signature observational wit; the draft replaces it with 'mascara melted like a skull face,' which is a different image with a different register and loses the dry humor of the original.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the source's 'undead look' phrasing, or preserve the dry clinical humor rather than substituting a more lurid image.

findings.source_passage: Blake snorted. The noise even sounded piggish.
findings.source_locator: During Blake's first appearance at the rear of the truck
findings.why_it_matters: The two-sentence deadpan—the second sentence as a standalone comic beat—is a stylistic signature of the narrator's ironic register; the draft renders it as 'He snorted, a wet, animal sound,' losing the wry self-awareness of the observation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-sentence structure: 'Blake snorted. The noise even sounded piggish.' The comic rhythm is the point.

findings.source_passage: Cindy charged Blake. He side-stepped her attack and smacked her on the back of her head. Cindy's eyes rolled back in her head, and she crumpled to the ground.
findings.source_locator: The fight scene at the rear of the truck
findings.why_it_matters: The source has the specific detail that Blake side-steps and smacks the back of Cindy's head, with 'eyes rolled back'—a kinetically precise beat; the draft replaces this with 'He stepped aside and clipped the back of her head. She folded to the ground like a dropped rag,' which changes the physical mechanics and imposes an uncharacteristic simile.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Cindy's eyes rolled back in her head' as it is the specific physical detail that conveys the violence; the 'dropped rag' simile is a drafting invention that doesn't belong.

findings.source_passage: A flash of red blinded my vision. I screamed and lunged at the closest asshole.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's 'I screamed and lunged' captures Miriam's impulsive rage; the draft omits the scream entirely ('I lunged shoulder-first'), softening the emotional intensity of her reaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I screamed and lunged' to preserve the involuntary emotional outburst that characterizes Miriam's personality.

findings.source_passage: A soft female voice spoke up. 'There is no problem.'
findings.why_it_matters: The source ends on bare dialogue with minimal attribution—maximum tension. The draft adds 'calm as a blade sliding free,' an editorializing simile that intrudes on the cliffhanger effect and imposes interpretation on what should be purely mysterious.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the added simile; end the chapter as the source does, on the spoken line alone.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium findings (opening voice register, the 'undead look' simile, and the piggish-snort comic beat) show consistent voice flattening that cumulatively dulls the narrator's wry register, but no single erasure rises to regeneration threshold.
